---
title: "Phase 4. Delivery, communication and sign-off"
description: "Deliver it with its caveats and get the approval it needs."
---

You deliver the analysis to your commissioner with its caveats attached, then get it signed off.

## What you do

{{< include /guidance/_partials/step-levels-key.qmd >}}

1. [Every level[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Deliver draft results to your commissioner first.**
2. [Every level[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Write the [quality assurance statement](../09-resources/r5-quality-assurance-statement.qmd)
   at every level.** It is short at Level 1, and from Level 3 you publish it with the output.
   It covers:
     - the assumptions, the uncertainty and the limitations
     - what the results can and cannot be used for
     - links to references, code and data

   From Level 3, it also carries:

     - the assurer, named, independent of the delivering team, with dates
     - confirmation that the code was assured against the
       [NHSBSA Analytical Code Assurance Playbook](https://nhsbsa-data-analytics.github.io/nhsbsa-analytical-code-assurance-playbook)
     - the uncertainty as a range, with its main source
     - the sensitivity testing result for the key assumption
     - the transparency record reference, where the tool is in scope
     - the approver and the next review date
3. [Every level[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Put material caveats beside the figure they qualify**, not in an annex.
4. [Every level[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Communicate findings, limitations and uncertainty clearly, objectively and impartially.**
   Quantify uncertainty where you can, and avoid unwarranted confidence in any one option.
5. [Every level[:]{.visually-hidden}]{.pb-level} **Get it signed off** by the person your level requires. See
   [who signs at each level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/what-your-level-requires.qmd#in-phase-4-delivery-communication-and-sign-off).
   - If an impact dimension scored 4, go to
     [Business Critical analysis, step 7](../08-business-critical/index.qmd#step-7-publish-what-was-checked).

## Say who the numbers cover, and how they could be misread

- **Who is not in the data.** If a group is under-represented or missing, say so beside the
  result, not only in the method note.
- **How this could be misread.** Name the wrong conclusion somebody could reasonably draw, and
  say plainly what the analysis does not support.

## Outputs of this phase

- The output, in a form that meets your audience's needs, including accessibility.
- The quality assurance statement, attached to it and published with it from Level 3.
- The sign-off, from the person your level requires.
- The project record, archived with the output and linked from it.

## Ready for Phase 5 when

- Your commissioner has confirmed it meets their need and understands its limitations.
- The statement is attached to the output rather than filed separately.
- The sign-off the level requires has happened.

## Who does what in this phase

| Role | In Phase 4 |
|---|---|
| **Analyst** | Write it up with the caveats in the output itself. Produce the quality assurance statement |
| **Critical friend** | State the assurance: appropriately scoped, executed, validated, verified and documented |
| **Commissioner** | Confirm it meets your need, apply its limitations, and approve it for release |
| **Analysis Senior Responsible Officer** | Business Critical work only. Review the assurance evidence, then approve as fit for its intended use |
